item: The keyword digest is built a batch at a time and groups its families over what the machine can hold, so two of the four machines that declined it on memory now run it, and a third was not measured
summary: Four of the 17 machines in the 2026-10-05/06 diagnostics declined keyword-log-digest.json on memory against an estimate that was right (1,062 MiB) about a design that did not need it: every survivor's metadata and signature were held at once, then build_families (+535 MiB transient) and a dict per family. The digest now builds entries a batch at a time (_DigestPass; memory stop every 2,000 entries as before), groups families over a memory-sized basis (a tenth of the available memory at 2.5 KB a keyword, floor 50,000, disclosed in families_provenance together with a note, and in the summary's own basis_is_whole_window and basis_per_language, when the window was cut) and takes the families summary from seven light fields of each family. The document is the old one apart from six added keys, four in families_provenance and two in families_summary (a differential harness over 12 random databases, a normalising copy of the shared script that sets those six aside); the rise at 410,000 entries was 1,057 MiB and is 330 with 2 GB free, 253 with 1.2 GB, 490 with 4 GB and 816 with 16 GB (27 timed runs). The gate's need estimate follows the same model (fixed 60 MiB + entries x 500 B + grouped x 2,500 B + the article arrays), and the bundle's deadline covers the batch loop. Prediction: OOS-12 and hP, whose readings the tests pin, now carry the digest (OOS-10's reading is not in the repository); OOS-11, which had 425 MiB free, still declines, and says so.
